# wso2is_flow (Resource)

Manages a flow that the Console's flow builder can also edit (WSO2 IS 7.2 and later). A flow is the self sign-up form and its steps, the password recovery flow, or the invited user registration flow. Use this resource to build a custom sign-up form.

In a flow, form fields map to claims, and executors do the work of each step. Examples of executors are `PasswordProvisioningExecutor`, `EmailOTPExecutor`, `UserProvisioningExecutor` and federated executors such as `GoogleExecutor`.

`steps` holds the same JSON document that the Console stores (`GET /api/server/v1/flow?flowType=...`). You can design the flow in the Console and copy it with the `wso2is_flow` data source, or write it with `jsonencode`.

When you destroy the resource, the provider turns the flow off and deletes it. By default, WSO2 IS 7.3.0 does not allow the API to delete the root organization's flow. In that case, the provider only turns the flow off. The server behaviour guide explains how to allow deletion. To import a flow, use its flow type.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Custom self-registration form with an extra attribute.
resource "wso2is_flow" "sign_up" {
  flow_type = "REGISTRATION"
  completion_configs = {
    isEmailVerificationEnabled = "false"
    isAutoLoginEnabled         = "true"
  }
  steps = jsonencode([
    {
      id       = "sign_up_form"
      type     = "VIEW"
      size     = { width = 350, height = 500 }
      position = { x = 300, y = 200 }
      data = {
        components = [
          { id = "heading", category = "DISPLAY", type = "TYPOGRAPHY", variant = "H3", config = { text = "Create your account" } },
          {
            id = "form", category = "BLOCK", type = "FORM", config = {}
            components = [
              { id = "username", category = "FIELD", type = "INPUT", variant = "TEXT", config = { type = "text", label = "Username", required = true, identifier = "http://wso2.org/claims/username" } },
              { id = "email", category = "FIELD", type = "INPUT", variant = "EMAIL", config = { type = "email", label = "Email", required = true, identifier = "http://wso2.org/claims/emailaddress" } },
              { id = "member_no", category = "FIELD", type = "INPUT", variant = "TEXT", config = { type = "text", label = "Membership number", required = false, identifier = "http://wso2.org/claims/membershipNumber" } },
              { id = "password", category = "FIELD", type = "INPUT", variant = "PASSWORD", config = { type = "password", label = "Password", required = true, identifier = "password" } },
              { id = "submit", category = "ACTION", type = "BUTTON", variant = "PRIMARY", config = { type = "submit", text = "Sign up" },
              action = { type = "EXECUTOR", executor = { name = "PasswordProvisioningExecutor" }, next = "END" } },
            ]
          },
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      id       = "END"
      type     = "END"
      size     = { width = 200, height = 100 }
      position = { x = 800, y = 200 }
      data     = { action = { type = "EXECUTOR", executor = { name = "UserProvisioningExecutor" } } }
    },
  ])
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `flow_type` (String) `REGISTRATION`, `PASSWORD_RECOVERY` or `INVITED_USER_REGISTRATION`.
- `steps` (String) The steps of the flow, as a JSON array. Each step has an `id`, a `type` (such as `VIEW`, `REDIRECTION` or `END`), a `size` and a `position` (its place in the Console's editor), and `data`. The `data.components` list holds the step's content: `TYPOGRAPHY` text, and `FORM` blocks with `INPUT` fields and `BUTTON`s. Each field's `config.identifier` is a claim URI, or `password` or `otp`. Each button has an `action`, for example `{ type = "EXECUTOR", executor = { name = ... }, next = <step id or "END"> }`. The last step is `{ id = "END", type = "END" }`.

### Optional

- `completion_configs` (Map of String) Settings that apply when the flow finishes, for example `isEmailVerificationEnabled`, `isAutoLoginEnabled`, `isAccountLockOnCreationEnabled` and `isFlowCompletionNotificationEnabled`. The values are the strings `"true"` and `"false"`. The provider only manages the keys that you list.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the flow replaces the older, built-in flow. For registration, this means that the flow builds the self sign-up page. The default is `true`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `flow_type`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_flow.sign_up REGISTRATION
```
